observations.original: S source capture is an almost rectangular cobalt mass with a very broad light cyan top/upper face, a sudden dark lower tier, two thin rectangular face patches and a near-black lower body. It reads as a plain extruded slab; little crafted stone structure survives at game scale.
observations.target: Large rounded interlocking stone courses, cobalt/azure midtones, pale cyan edge turns, deep narrow seams and a few smaller nested stones. The stacked construction and varied broad facets give readable volume; tiny texture is restrained. The concept is a tall front face and alone does not certify native camera, root, height or the west connector.
observations.styleReference: Plant reference has soft broad light, warm rich material color, rounded crafted edge bands, clear planar turns and contained local contact darkness. It supports soft cartoon construction rather than sharp photographic noise.
observations.sourceCollection: Actual b176 collection S33_PROP_rock-wall-end.001 has a root and six meshes: full-cell continuous crag, broad contact shoulder, three face facets and finished east-end strata. Declared single west connector at local(-0.5,0,0), footprint1x1, height1.17, static one frame12fps. Old mesh/part counts and rectangle decorations are descriptive, not locked.

initialDesiredOutcomes: Replace large inert slab areas with readable interlocking broad stone volumes and deliberate larger/smaller rhythm.
Use coherent cobalt blues with luminous but controlled rounded edge turns, medium blue faces and narrow local seam darkness; avoid the original near-black lower dead area.
Make east termination look intentionally finished while west cut profile remains functional; carry detail coherently to reverse views.
Judge all4 registered native facings, logical and phone-scale read and independently captured middle joins before approval.
technicalCautions: The source blend opens with a generic library export scene/camera/resolution, so its active scene is not a valid per-asset capture contract.
Initial matrix-world bounds of hidden/unlinked facet objects require update/evaluated transform handling before numerical contract.
Source camera captureScale4 differs from catalog sourceScale2; this likely represents supersampling/downsample and must be reproduced rather than normalized by fitting.
